requirement: Parse an inventory command line with a required subcommand, an export command whose --json and --csv flags are mutually exclusive and whose --limit must be a positive integer defaulting to 100, and return exit code 2 for usage errors instead of exiting the process.
skeleton: positive_int argparse type, build_parser with required subparsers and a mutually exclusive group, and main catching SystemExit and printing the chosen action.
caption: A testable command line built with the standard-library argparse module. positive_int(text) converts the text with int and raises argparse.ArgumentTypeError saying it is not a positive integer both when conversion fails, chained from the ValueError, and when the value is below one. build_parser creates a parser named inv whose subparsers use dest command and are required, so running with no subcommand is a usage error. The export subcommand takes a positional path, a mutually exclusive group holding the store_true flags --json and --csv, and --limit using positive_int with a default of 100; the count subcommand takes nothing. main(argv, out) parses argv and catches the SystemExit that argparse raises on errors, returning its integer code, or EXIT_USAGE of 2 when the code is not an integer, instead of letting the process exit. For count it prints count to out; for export it prints export, the path, as csv when --csv was given or json otherwise, and the limit, and returns 0. The fixture asserts that export items.db prints json with limit 100, that --csv --limit 5 prints csv with limit 5, that --json with --csv returns 2 with argparse's not allowed with argument message, that --limit 0 returns 2 naming the value and many also returns 2, that no subcommand returns 2, and that count prints count.

plan.intent: Parse an inventory command line and report exit codes
constraints: --limit must be a positive integer, rejected with argparse.ArgumentTypeError, and defaults to 100
Usage errors return exit code 2 from main instead of raising SystemExit

rationale.teaches: Required subparsers, a mutually exclusive group, a custom type raising ArgumentTypeError, and converting SystemExit into a return code.
rationale.why: Command-line parsers fail quietly when flags that should conflict are both accepted, when limits accept zero or when a missing subcommand slips through, and only exact argv cases catch that.

ops.docstring: Inventory command line with subcommands, exclusive format flags and exit codes.

candidates.why_wrong: The limit check only rejects negatives, so --limit 0 is accepted.
The format is chosen from the --json flag, so --csv still exports json.
A plain argument group does not make the flags exclusive, so --json with --csv is accepted.
The limit defaults to 10 instead of 100.
Subcommands are optional, so an empty command line falls through to export and crashes instead of returning 2.
